directAnswer: To create a restore point in Windows, open the System Properties, navigate to the System Protection tab, and click on 'Create'.
summary: Creating a restore point allows you to revert your system to a previous state in case of issues.

sections.heading: System Requirements
sections.body: Ensure that System Protection is enabled for the drive where Windows is installed. This is usually the C: drive.

sections.heading: Creating a Restore Point
sections.body: Follow the steps below to create a restore point in Windows.

sections.heading: Restoration Process
sections.body: Learn how to restore your system using the restore point you created.

steps.title: Open System Properties
steps.detail: Right-click on 'This PC' or 'Computer' on the desktop or in File Explorer and select 'Properties'.

steps.title: Access System Protection
steps.detail: In the System window, click on 'System protection' in the left sidebar.

steps.title: Create a Restore Point
steps.detail: In the System Protection tab, click on the 'Create' button, enter a description, and click 'Create' again.

steps.title: Confirmation
steps.detail: Wait for the confirmation message that the restore point has been created successfully.

faqs.question: How often should I create restore points?
faqs.answer: It's recommended to create restore points before major system changes, such as updates or software installations.

faqs.question: Can I delete old restore points?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can manage and delete old restore points through the System Protection settings.

faqs.question: What happens if I run out of disk space for restore points?
faqs.answer: Windows will automatically delete the oldest restore points to free up space for new ones.

caveats: Restore points do not back up personal files; they only affect system files and settings.
